ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOB = 30^\circ$, point $P$ is a fixed point inside $\angle AOB$ and $OP=3$. If points $M$ and $N$ are moving points on rays $OA$ and $OB$ different from point $O$, respectively, what is the minimum perimeter of $\triangle PMN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, let $E$ and $D$ be the symmetric points of point $P$ with respect to $OA$ and $OB$, respectively. Draw lines $DN$, $EM$, $DE$, $OD$, and $OE$,\\
then $OA$ perpendicularly bisects $PE$, and $OB$ perpendicularly bisects $PD$,\\
$\therefore EM=PM$, $DN=PN$, $OD=OP=OE=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ is $PM+MN+PN=EM+MN+DN$,\\
As the shortest distance between two points is a straight line, when points $E$, $M$, $N$, $D$ are collinear, the value of $EM+MN+DN$ is minimized, and the minimum value is the length of $DE$,\\
$\because OE=OP$ and $OA\perp PE$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOE=\angle AOP$ (angle-side-angle congruence in isosceles triangle),\\
Similarly, it can be obtained: $\angle BOD=\angle BOP$,\\
$\because \angle AOB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOP+\angle AOP=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DOE=\angle BOD+\angle BOP+\angle AOP+\angle AOE=2\left(\angle BOP+\angle AOP\right)=60^\circ$,\\
And since $OD=OE=3$,\\
$\therefore \triangle DOE$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore DE=OD=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of $EM+MN+DN$ is 3,\\
$\therefore$ the minimum perimeter of $\triangle PMN$ is $\boxed{3}$,

Because M is on the axis of symmetry OA, PM=EM; because N is on the axis of symmetry OB, PN=DN. Therefore the perimeter of triangle PMN is PM+MN+PN=EM+MN+DN. In triangle EOD, OE=OD=3, and the included angle ∠EOD=60°, so triangle EOD is an equilateral triangle, DE=3. Therefore the minimum perimeter of triangle PMN is 3.
